Yes. On 16 June the plant exceeded its 1250 kW contract limit twice, in the 08:00–08:15 window:

- Peak: 1324.4 kW at 08:15 [data: get_demand]
- 08:00: 1307.1 kW and 08:15: 1324.4 kW — both above the 1250 kW contract (1.06×) [data: get_demand]

This is the "Monday morning simultaneous start" scenario (S2): demand jumped from ~540 kW at 07:45 to ~1307 kW at 08:00 as machines started at once. It cleared by 08:30 (1239 kW) and stayed below contract for the rest of the day.

Whether this triggers a penalty depends on the tariff's demand penalty rule, which I can look up if you want the exact charge.

According to SOP-02, a reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating (25.2 kW) continuously, so leaving it in standby burns real energy while producing nothing. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend.

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend: weekend energy was about 1,556 kWh versus about 346 kWh normal, an excess of about 1,210 kWh from that single oven. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

I now have both the shed order and the never-shed list.

**First shed:** EV charging (EV-01), paused first because it has no effect on production [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].

The full shed order (least disruptive first): EV-01 pause 100% → burn-in loading BI-01/BI-02 delay 35% → chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01/CH-02) 4% → compressed-air pressure −0.5 bar (AC-01–AC-03) 3.5%. Restoration is in reverse order [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].

**Never shed:** server room (DC-01), running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04), and reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed].
